title: Open a row of breaker terminals, lower a comb busbar into all at once, then screw each terminal down onto its pin
instruction: Fit the comb busbar to the three breakers: open their top terminals, lower the comb's pins into all three, tighten the terminal screws, then put the screwdriver down and move both hands away.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00) list as Core tasks 'Connect wires to circuit breakers, transformers, or other components.' and 'Assemble, install, test, or maintain electrical or electronic wiring, equipment, appliances, apparatus, or fixtures, using hand tools or power tools.' A row of DIN-rail breakers in a control panel or distribution board is commonly fed by a pin comb busbar. The maker's steps (Contactum consumer unit instructions): 'Loosen the MCB terminal screws. Fit the busbar and tighten the terminal screws.' A breaker's terminal clamp is shut until its screw is backed out, and a rigid comb fits only when every clamp in the row is open: so each screw is backed out with a plain screwdriver in wrist strokes, the bit kept in the head, the comb's pins are lowered into all the open terminals at once in one straight push, and each screw is driven back down onto its pin.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A painted steel mounting plate (24 x 19.5 cm) stands upright at x 38, on a wooden board behind it, with a 35 mm DIN rail across it 15 cm up. On the rail, three single-pole miniature circuit breakers of one range (Acti9 iC60N type, modelled 85 x 18 x 73 mm, 18 mm pitch), fronts at x 30, centred at y -2.7, -0.9 and 0.9. Each has its line terminal in its top: a box clamp 10 x 8 mm, 14 mm deep, closed by an M5 screw in the front face 13 mm below the top (0.8 mm a turn; about 3.75 turns out to clear a pin). A pin comb busbar of the same range, cut to four pins: an insulated bar 76 x 10 x 12 mm with a copper strip, four copper pins 3 x 6 x 13 mm at 18 mm pitch, 50 g, resting on two thin wooden posts at (21.5, 16), its bar 10 cm up. A plain #2 Pozidriv screwdriver (handle 32 mm across and 60 mm long, 50 mm shaft, 60 g) lies from x 22.5 to 33.5 at y -15.5 in a steel V-stand whose rests are at x 24.7 to 28.7, its axis 17 cm up, handle towards the arms.
scoring: Read from video and a check by hand. 0 once the comb or the screwdriver has fallen off the table. 0.03 for each terminal opened: its screw backed out far enough for a pin (3.7 turns; in a real trial a 3 mm gauge pin drops in), counted once it has been. 0.25 more while the comb is home: all three pins in their clamps (in front of the jaws) and its bar down on the breakers' tops (within 1.5 mm: a 1.5 mm feeler gauge does not pass under it), square in plan (within 3 degrees, by try square). 0.1 more for each screw down, driven onto its pin and clamping it (in a real trial: it turns no further by fingers): 0.64 with all three. 1.0 when all three are down, every fingertip of both hands is at least 5 cm from the whole comb and 4 cm from the whole screwdriver, the screwdriver's tip is at least 2 cm from the screw heads, and a 10 N pull up along the pins, by spring balance, moves the comb less than 1 mm (dial gauge), all held for 2 s (hands' distances from the film against a tape; the hold by the film's timer); a pull that moves it more leaves the partial score.
reset_notes: Back each terminal screw down onto an empty clamp, lift the comb out and lay it on its posts, and lay the screwdriver in its stand. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on GPU. The thread is code: the screwdriver's turn turns a screw only with its bit's tip on the head's face, square within 10 degrees; the clamp follows at 0.8 mm a turn and, driven home, presses its pin with about 10 N (the maker's 2 N m is not reached). Breakers modelled 85 x 18 x 73 mm (the maker's 91 x 18 x 78.5); comb pin size approximated until measured. The screw heads have no collider: the bit on a head is read in code.
